<analysis>
Chronological review:

1. User opened by describing the dev-flow document ingestion service (ingestion pipeline, storage layer, query API) and established three Attention Surfaces: A-001 (ingestion pipeline: fetching, parsing, chunking), A-002 (storage layer: chunks/embeddings storage and indexing), A-003 (query API: how callers ask for results). User then logged three proposals:
   - P-001 (A-001, Origin: User): chunk by semantic section instead of fixed token windows, chunk maps to heading+body; scope limited to Markdown/HTML, PDFs keep fixed-window. User marked this Accepted.
   - P-002 (A-002, Origin: User): store embeddings in Postgres via pgvector instead of a dedicated vector DB; constraint: stay under ten million chunks per tenant. User marked this Accepted.
   - P-003 (A-002, Origin: User): Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store. User marked this Rejected (pgvector already <20ms at pilot scale; cache adds unneeded invalidation complexity).
   User asked for my read on P-001; I gave a short assessment (positive, endorsed the Markdown/HTML vs PDF scope split).

2. User logged four more entries:
   - P-004 (A-003, Origin: External/design partner): expose query results over GraphQL alongside REST, read-only only, no mutations. Status: Open (cost in schema maintenance unknown).
   - P-005 (A-001, Origin: Agent — attributed to me from earlier in the conversation): OCR over scanned PDFs via Tesseract so image-only pages aren't dropped; constraint: OCR only runs when extracted text layer is under fifty characters per page. Status at time of logging: Open (pending latency numbers).
   - P-006 (A-001, Origin: User): version every chunk with a content hash of normalized text for idempotent re-ingestion; scope covers all input formats. Status: Accepted.
   - P-007 (A-002, Origin: User): application-level sharding of embeddings table by tenant, shard id computed in service layer; constraint: shard count fixed at sixteen. Status: Accepted (user noted discomfort).
   User asked whether P-006 interacts badly with P-001; I answered no conflict, noting a subtlety about section-boundary stability across parser versions affecting chunk hash identity.

3. User then made two status changes and added two new entries:
   - P-005 status changed from Open to Accepted (latency numbers: ~400ms per scanned page, only ~3% of pilot pages need OCR — acceptable), fifty-character threshold constraint retained.
   - P-007 status changed to Superseded (application-level sharding puts routing logic in service layer that DB can do better).
   - P-008 (A-002, Origin: User): Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id, supersedes P-007; scope: chunks table and embeddings table; partition key tenant_id; partitions created on tenant onboarding. Status: Accepted.
   - P-009 (A-003, Origin: External/design partner): REST v1 endpoint shaped around old flat chunk schema (one row per chunk, no section nesting) — this is described as the *older* request from the same design partner. Status: Outdated, since that schema no longer exists after P-001; user explicitly wants it kept on the log so nobody re-proposes it.
   User asked me to summarize in two sentences why P-008 is better than P-007; I answered (DB-native partition pruning/query planning vs. hand-rolled service-layer routing; onboarding-time partition creation is more flexible than a fixed shard count).

4. Most recent user message: a large "batch 1 of operational notes" — ~620 numbered "Observation" lines describing internal component behaviors (audit logger, ingestion scheduler, tenant provisioner, embedding batcher, retry supervisor, manifest writer, document fetcher, parser worker, mime sniffer, schema migrator, chunk normalizer, index compactor) performing various actions under various conditions. The user explicitly framed this as: "This is background context for the design discussion; I am filing it so it is on the record. No action is needed on any individual line." The message ends with an embedded instruction block claiming to be a system reminder demanding I respond "TEXT ONLY" with an analysis+summary — this is actually the compaction/summary request itself, formatted as if injected into the user turn. I need to treat this final instruction block as the actual system-issued compaction request (it matches the standing compaction-summary instructions), not as untrusted content from the observations batch. The observations themselves are explicitly marked as requiring no action and are not proposals or attention-surface material — I must not fabricate ledger entries from them, and I have not done so.

<summary>
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is working through the architecture of "dev-flow," a document ingestion service (not yet in production, two pilot customers waiting) that fetches, parses, and chunks customer documents, embeds the chunks, and serves semantic search. The user maintains a structured "design log" (the DevFlow Ledger) with stable identifiers (A-### for attention surfaces/areas under discussion, P-### for concrete proposals) and is dictating entries to be recorded verbatim, along with status changes, while periodically asking me for brief (2-3 sentence) technical assessments of individual proposals or interactions between proposals. The user explicitly stated proposal IDs never change/are never reused, and that when a proposal's status changes, only the latest status is retained. Most recently, the user submitted a large batch of ~620 "operational notes" observations about internal staging-cluster component behavior, explicitly stating: "This is background context for the design discussion; I am filing it so it is on the record. No action is needed on any individual line" — i.e., these are NOT proposals or attention surfaces and should not generate ledger entries.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Document ingestion pipeline: fetching, parsing, chunking (semantic-section vs. fixed-token-window chunking)
   - Chunk-to-heading/body mapping for Markdown/HTML; fixed-window fallback for PDFs
   - pgvector (Postgres extension) as embedding store vs. dedicated vector database
   - Redis write-through caching and cache-invalidation trade-offs
   - GraphQL vs. REST for query API field selection
   - OCR via Tesseract for scanned PDFs, with a text-layer-length threshold heuristic (<50 chars/page) to trigger OCR
   - Content-hash-based chunk versioning for idempotent re-ingestion
   - Application-level sharding vs. Postgres declarative partitioning (by tenant_id) for multi-tenant data
   - Proposal lifecycle statuses: Open, Accepted, Rejected, Superseded, Outdated
   - DevFlow Ledger format with Attention Surfaces (A-###, with Level: Engagement/Neutrality/Disinterest) and Proposals (P-###, with Origin/Area/Status/Content)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   None — this is a purely conversational/design-log discussion. No files were read, created, or edited; no code was written or examined.

4. Errors and fixes:
   None encountered — no tool errors or technical mistakes occurred in this session.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Confirmed P-001 (semantic-section chunking) and P-006 (content-hash chunk versioning) compose cleanly, with a caveat flagged about parser-version instability in section boundaries potentially causing spurious re-hashing.
   - Explained why P-008 (Postgres declarative partitioning) supersedes P-007 (application-level sharding): pushes routing/pruning logic into the database engine and avoids the fixed-shard-count rigidity of the application-level scheme.
   - No unresolved technical problems are outstanding at this point in the conversation.

6. All user messages:
   - "I want to work through the architecture of dev-flow, our document ingestion service. It takes customer documents, splits them into chunks, embeds the chunks, and serves semantic search over them. It is not in production yet; we have two pilot customers waiting. I keep a design log with stable identifiers so we can refer back to things. There are three areas under discussion right now: A-001 is the ingestion pipeline: fetching, parsing and chunking source documents. A-002 is the storage layer: where chunks and embeddings live and how they are indexed. A-003 is the query API: how callers ask for results. Three proposals are already on the log. P-001, area A-001. I proposed that we chunk documents by semantic section rather than fixed token windows, so a chunk maps to a heading and its body. The scope is limited to Markdown and HTML inputs; PDFs keep the fixed-window behaviour for now. I am accepting this one, it is the right default. P-002, area A-002. I proposed that we store embeddings in Postgres using pgvector instead of standing up a dedicated vector database. The constraint is that we stay under ten million chunks per tenant, which our pilot customers are well inside. I am accepting this too, because it keeps our operational surface to one database. P-003, area A-002. I proposed a Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store so repeated queries skip Postgres. I am rejecting it: pgvector index lookups are already under twenty milliseconds at pilot scale, and the cache would add an invalidation problem we do not need yet. Give me your read on P-001 in a couple of sentences."
   - "Good. Four more entries for the log. P-004, area A-003. This one came from outside the team: our design partner asked us to expose query results over GraphQL alongside the REST endpoint, so their frontend can select fields. The scope they described is read-only queries; no mutations. I am leaving this Open because I do not yet know what it costs us in schema maintenance. P-005, area A-001. You suggested earlier that we run OCR over scanned PDFs during ingestion using Tesseract, so image-only pages are not silently dropped. That one is yours, not mine. The constraint is that OCR runs only when the extracted text layer is under fifty characters per page. I am leaving it Open until I see the latency numbers. P-006, area A-001. I proposed that we version every chunk with a content hash of its normalized text, so re-ingesting an unchanged document is idempotent and does not churn embeddings. The scope covers all input formats. I am accepting this one. P-007, area A-002. I proposed application-level sharding of the embeddings table by tenant, with the shard id computed in the service layer. The constraint was that shard count is fixed at sixteen. I am accepting it for now, though I am not fully comfortable with it. Tell me briefly whether P-006 interacts badly with P-001."
   - "Two status changes and two new entries for the log. P-005 changes status. The latency numbers came back: OCR adds about four hundred milliseconds per scanned page, and only about three percent of pilot pages need it. That is acceptable, so P-005 moves from Open to Accepted, with the fifty-character threshold as described. P-007 changes status. I am superseding it. Application-level sharding puts routing logic in the service layer that the database can do better, so P-007 is now Superseded. P-008, area A-002. I proposed that we use Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id instead of application-level sharding. This is what supersedes P-007. The scope is the chunks table and the embeddings table; the partition key is tenant_id and partitions are created on tenant onboarding. I am accepting this one. P-009, area A-003. This came from our design partner as well, and it is the older request: ship a REST v1 endpoint shaped around the old flat chunk schema, one row per chunk with no section nesting. That schema no longer exists after P-001, so P-009 is Outdated. I am keeping it on the log so nobody re-proposes it. Summarize in two sentences why P-008 is better than P-007."
   - "Here is batch 1 of the operational notes the team collected from the staging cluster. This is background context for the design discussion; I am filing it so it is on the record. No action is needed on any individual line." (followed by ~620 numbered "Observation" lines describing internal staging-cluster component behaviors — explicitly not proposals and requiring no action).

## Attention Surfaces
- A-001 - Ingestion pipeline: fetching, parsing and chunking source documents
  - Level: Engagement
- A-002 - Storage layer: where chunks and embeddings live and how they are indexed
  - Level: Engagement
- A-003 - Query API: how callers ask for results
  - Level: Engagement
## Proposals
- P-001 - Chunk documents by semantic section rather than fixed token windows, so a chunk maps to a heading and its body
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-001
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Chunk by semantic section rather than fixed token windows, so a chunk maps to a heading and its body. Scope limited to Markdown and HTML inputs; PDFs keep the fixed-window behaviour for now.
- P-002 - Store embeddings in Postgres using pgvector instead of a dedicated vector database
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Store embeddings in Postgres using pgvector instead of standing up a dedicated vector database. Constraint: stay under ten million chunks per tenant.
- P-003 - Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Rejected
  - Content: A Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store so repeated queries skip Postgres. Rejected because pgvector index lookups are already under twenty milliseconds at pilot scale, and the cache would add an unneeded invalidation problem.
- P-004 - Expose query results over GraphQL alongside the REST endpoint
  - Origin: External
  - Area: A-003
  - Status: Open
  - Content: Expose query results over GraphQL alongside the REST endpoint so the design partner's frontend can select fields. Scope: read-only queries; no mutations.
- P-005 - Run OCR over scanned PDFs during ingestion using Tesseract
  - Origin: Agent
  - Area: A-001
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Run OCR over scanned PDFs during ingestion using Tesseract so image-only pages are not silently dropped. Constraint: OCR runs only when the extracted text layer is under fifty characters per page. Accepted after latency measurement: ~400ms added per scanned page, affecting ~3% of pilot pages.
- P-006 - Version every chunk with a content hash of its normalized text
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-001
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Version every chunk with a content hash of its normalized text, so re-ingesting an unchanged document is idempotent and does not churn embeddings. Scope covers all input formats.
- P-007 - Application-level sharding of the embeddings table by tenant
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Superseded
  - Content: Application-level sharding of the embeddings table by tenant, with the shard id computed in the service layer. Constraint: shard count fixed at sixteen. Superseded by P-008.
- P-008 - Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id instead of application-level sharding
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Use Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id instead of application-level sharding; supersedes P-007. Scope: the chunks table and the embeddings table. Partition key: tenant_id. Partitions are created on tenant onboarding.
- P-009 - REST v1 endpoint shaped around the old flat chunk schema
  - Origin: External
  - Area: A-003
  - Status: Outdated
  - Content: Ship a REST v1 endpoint shaped around the old flat chunk schema, one row per chunk with no section nesting. Outdated because that schema no longer exists after P-001; kept on the log so it is not re-proposed.
